name: Lazy ML
summary: Lazily evaluated, strongly typed dialect of ML developed at Chalmers in the early 1980s; its compiler introduced the G-machine for compiling lazy graph reduction to native code and later became the basis of HBC, one of the first Haskell compilers.

level_notes.0: The Chalmers LML compiler (written mostly in LML itself) was distributed with HBC; no maintained public source repository is known.
level_notes.1: Defined by the Chalmers papers (LFP 1984, Computer Journal 1989); publisher pages report blocked from the sandbox.
